title.value: An Atari Model Zoo for Analyzing, Visualizing, and Comparing Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents
title.justification: This is the exact title mentioned under the Abstract section of the paper.
title.quote: This paper introduces the Atari Zoo framework, which contains models trained across benchmark Atari games, in an easy-to-use format, as well as code that im- plements common modes of analysis and connects such models to a popular neural network visual- ization library.

analysis.description: The paper presents the Atari Zoo framework aimed at easing the analysis, visualization, and comparison of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents. By training multiple DRL algorithms at scale and integrating previously released models, the paper releases models and code to facilitate understanding and examining learned representations of DRL algorithms. It emphasizes the potential of this resource by providing initial analyses on the performance and representations of several DRL algorithms.

type.justification: The paper involves training several algorithms, analyzing and visualizing them, which involves empirical work.
type.quote: We lessen this friction, by (1) training several algorithms at scale and releasing trained models, (2) integrating with a previous DRL model release, and (3) releas- ing code that makes it easy for anyone to load, visualize, and analyze such models.

name.justification: The paper focuses on understanding and analyzing deep reinforcement learning agents.
name.quote: Much human and computational effort has aimed to improve how deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms perform on benchmarks such as the Atari Learning Environment.

name.justification: The paper focuses on visualizing and interpreting the behavior of DRL agents.
name.quote: The hope is to gain more insight into how DNNs are representing information, motivated both to enable more interpretable decisions from these models [Olah et al., 2018] and to illuminate previously unknown properties about DNNs [Yosinski et al., 2015].

name.justification: A2C is one of the DRL algorithms analyzed in the paper.
name.quote: To demonstrate the promise of this model zoo and software, this paper presents an initial analysis of the products of seven DRL algorithms spanning policy gradient, value-based, and evolutionary methods: A2C (policy-gradient; [Mnih et al., 2016])

is_contributed.justification: A2C is sourced and used in the analysis, not newly developed in this paper.
is_contributed.quote: the particular algorithms chosen to train included two policy gradients algorithms (A2C [Mnih et al., 2016] and IMPALA [Espeholt et al., 2018])

is_executed.justification: The A2C model is part of the trained algorithms in the paper.
is_executed.quote: To demonstrate the promise of this model zoo and software, this paper presents an initial analysis... A2C (policy-gradient; [Mnih et al., 2016])

is_compared.justification: The A2C model is compared against other DRL models like DQN and Rainbow.
is_compared.quote: The analysis illuminates differences in learned policies across methods that are independent of raw score performance.
